items.title: CloudOrbit launches Monday August 3, 2026
items.body:
CloudOrbit is now available — the AWS session manager you wish Leapp was.

## What's included

- **AWS SSO** — switch accounts without touching a config file
- **Auto-kubeconfig** — EKS clusters detected and written automatically
- **Session persistence** — active sessions survive app restarts
- **Region selector** — pick any AWS region per profile
- **IAM / Chained / Federated** — all auth methods supported
- **Cloudflare & corporate proxy** compatible

Free. Native Rust. No Electron.

items.title: DataOrbit launches Monday August 3, 2026
items.body:
DataOrbit is the DynamoDB GUI the AWS console never was.

## What's included

- **Browse** — grid + JSON views, row detail panel, schema inspector
- **Explore** — query builder with GSI support, filter expressions, cost warnings
- **Live Streams** — real-time DynamoDB Streams event viewer
- **Cross-table joins** — inner, left, left-anti, right, right-anti
- **Query history** — full history with search
- **CouchDB** support
- **No Electron, no JVM** — pure Rust + Tauri

Free forever. MIT licensed.

items.title: Mermaid Preview v0.1.2
items.body:
## What's new

- Bug fixes and stability improvements for JCEF panel
- Better handling of malformed mermaid blocks (no more frozen preview)
- Mermaid 10.9.3 bundled — works fully offline / air-gapped

items.title: CloudOrbit + DataOrbit launch Monday August 3
items.body:
Two apps, one day. **CloudOrbit** (AWS session manager) and **DataOrbit** (DynamoDB GUI) both go live on **Monday August 3, 2026**.

- CloudOrbit: AWS SSO, EKS, kubeconfig auto-update, works behind Cloudflare
- DataOrbit: live streams, cross-table joins, query builder with GSI support

Both are free, native Rust, open source.

items.title: WattsOrbit v1.3.0
items.body:
## What's new

- **NewsBell** in the tray popup — unread dot and release notes dropdown
- **News screen** in the Dashboard with markdown rendering and pull-to-refresh
- **UpdaterModal** — changelog, download progress, in-app install
- **Homebrew Cask** auto-updates on every release

items.title: BastionOrbit — public launch later in 2026
items.body:
BastionOrbit has been moved off its July 3 slot. The auto-expiry TTL flow and multi-bastion connectivity probe need more soak time before going public.

- One-click port forwarding through bastion hosts
- Auto-expiry TTL — never leave a tunnel open overnight
- Multi-bastion management with connectivity probing
- Pairs with DataOrbit for tunneled DB connections

Real `ssh -N -L` processes — no protocol reimplementation. Free forever. Sign up for the launch date drop.

items.title: klight — public launch later in 2026
items.body:
klight has been moved off the May 29 slot. The three-world rollout (Solo dev, Startup team, Remote cluster) needs more soak time before going public — we'd rather ship it right than ship it on a deadline.

- Full-stack Kubernetes envs in two commands
- Postgres, Kafka, Redis spin up in the right order
- Each developer gets their own namespace
- Local minikube, team sync, or remote EKS / GKE / AKS — same CLI

Open source under MIT. Sign up to get notified the moment a launch date is locked.

items.title: ProxyOrbit — public launch later in 2026
items.body:
ProxyOrbit doesn't have a public launch date yet — the MITM cert chain and Zscaler workaround flow need another QA pass before going public.

- Capture HTTP/HTTPS from any Mac app
- Filter by method, status, host, path
- Real-time request log with body inspection
- Native Rust + Hyper + Tokio — under 30 MB at idle

No subscription, no $50 license. MIT. Sign up to get notified the moment a date is locked.

items.title: Switch between AWS accounts in seconds
items.body:
Running multiple AWS accounts? CloudOrbit cycles through all active sessions in the sidebar every 5 seconds — click any indicator to jump directly to that session.

Use the region selector per profile to avoid switching regions manually in the terminal.

items.title: Speed up queries — always use a GSI
items.body:
Scanning large DynamoDB tables is slow and expensive. In DataOrbit's Explore tab, open the **Index** dropdown to pick a GSI — filter fields update automatically to match the index keys.

Always prefer a GSI query over a Scan when you know the access pattern.

items.title: Keep the tray popup open
items.body: Hold ⌥ (Option) while clicking the menu-bar icon and the popup stays pinned — useful when you want to watch wattage drift while doing something else.
